Interesting — react-hook-form 7.87.0 is installed (a fresh resolution of ^7.62.0 → 7.87.0, released later). The TS error is about `UseFormHandleSubmit` type incompatibility — a type-level issue with a newer version of react-hook-form.

But wait — why did the main frontend build succeed on the same lockfile? In the main build, `npm ci` used the same lockfile... RHF should resolve to the same 7.87.0 in both builds. And the main build's `tsc` for shell succeeded?!

Hmm, let me check the main frontend2 log for the shell build. The main build ran `npm run build:release --workspace=shell` = `tsc && vite build`. Let me check whether it actually ran tsc and passed... The frontend image built successfully, and shell/dist existed (index.html in /usr/share/nginx/html). So tsc passed in the main build.

The difference between the main build and the standalone: the standalone uses `npm ci --workspace shell --include-workspace-root=false`. With `--include-workspace-root=false`, only the shell workspace's dependencies get installed (and shared? no — only the explicitly specified workspaces... actually `npm ci --workspace shell` installs the deps for the root + shell). Hmm.

What could differ: maybe the tsc error depends on which version of `@types/react` or react-hook-form's types... If `npm ci --workspace shell --include-workspace-root=false` installed a different (older/newer) version than a full `npm ci`? The lockfile pins everything to the same version — npm ci always installs the lockfile versions for the selected workspaces. So RHF is 7.87.0 in both.

Wait — maybe the main build didn't actually type-check successfully... Let me check the frontend2 log for shell's tsc output. `build:release` = `tsc && vite build`. If tsc had failed, the whole RUN would have failed (set -e inside the for loop — in my batched RUN, shell was the last step without & — `npm run build:release --workspace=shell` — a failure would fail the entire RUN). The frontend built OK, so shell's tsc+build passed in the main build.

Differences between main and standalone:
1. Main: full `npm ci` (all workspaces). Standalone: `npm ci --workspace shell --include-workspace-root=false`.
2. This could change the hoisting of @types/react! In the full install, @types/react might be hoisted from a different version... All workspace @types/react: let me check the versions. If shell pins @types/react ^19.1.11 and another workspace pins a different version, npm will nest the differing one. With the subset install, resolution/hoisting could pick a different @types/react version → different type compatibility → TS2322.

Actually, a more likely factor for TS2322: react-hook-form's type compatibility with @types/react / react's types. RHF 7.87.0 + @types/react 19.x... this error pattern (UseFormHandleSubmit type mismatch) is a known issue with RHF 7.87+ and specific @types/react versions.

The standalone install has different hoisting → shell picks up a different @types/react (possibly a nested one from the lockfile for another workspace) → type error.

This is a workspace-isolation issue in the sub-MFE Dockerfile (a pre-existing repo inconsistency: mfe-fp/mfe-ewm's Dockerfiles pass `--workspace mfe-ewm --workspace shared`, but mfe-ws/shell only pass one workspace + the build script is also different).

The main frontend Dockerfile — the documented primary frontend build ("build the main Dockerfile", "via Docker (recommended)") — builds all workspaces with a full `npm ci`, and it succeeds. The sub-MFE Dockerfiles are alternative per-MFE images, and mfe-ws/shell's Dockerfiles are missing the shared-workspace handling that mfe-fp/mfe-ewm have.

What to do:
- mfe-ws: missing `--workspace shared` in npm ci and the `npm run -w shared build` step. Add both (following the pattern of mfe-fp/mfe-ewm).
- shell: has build:dep (builds shared) in its build script, but npm ci is missing `--workspace shared` → shared's devDeps (vite, etc.) might not be installed at the correct hoisted level... Actually, shared is a workspace dependency of shell ("shared": "*") — npm installs workspace links + their dependencies. Hmm, `npm ci --workspace shell` should install shared's dependencies (as a dep of shell)...
